problem: SSRF. `fetch_report` now passes a URL supplied by the caller straight to `requests.get`. The diff removed both the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` allowlist and the fixed `https://api.internal.example` base URL, so the server will fetch any URL it is given and return the response body.
failure: Call `fetch_report('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/')` (or `http://localhost:6379/` or `http://10.0.0.5/admin`). The server makes the request from inside the network and returns `resp.content`, which leaks cloud credentials or internal service data. Under base, any host other than api.internal.example raised `ValueError('host not allowed')`.
fix: Restore the fixed base URL and the host allowlist. If full URLs must be accepted, parse the URL, require the https scheme, and require the hostname to be in `ALLOWED_HOSTS` before making the request.

problem: The https scheme is no longer enforced. The old code always built an `https://` URL; the new code accepts any scheme `requests` supports, including plain http.
failure: `fetch_report('http://api.internal.example/report')` sends the request in cleartext, so the report can be read or tampered with on the network. Plain-http internal services also become reachable.
fix: Reject any URL whose `urlparse(url).scheme` is not `'https'`.

problem: `requests.get` follows redirects by default. Now that the caller controls the URL, a host check applied only to the first URL can be bypassed with a redirect.
failure: With an allowlist restored, `fetch_report('https://cdn.example/r?to=http://169.254.169.254/')` returns a 302 from an open redirect on an allowed host. `requests` follows it to the internal target without any host check.
fix: Pass `allow_redirects=False`, or check the host again on every redirect hop.

problem: The hostname is never resolved and checked against private, loopback or link-local IP ranges. A domain the attacker controls that resolves to an internal IP, or DNS rebinding, gets around any check based only on the host string.
failure: `fetch_report('http://attacker.example/')` where the attacker's A record points to 127.0.0.1 or 10.x.x.x: the request reaches the internal host.
fix: Resolve the hostname, reject non-public IPs, and connect to the IP that was checked.

problem: `resp.content` reads the whole response into memory with no size limit, and `timeout=10` applies to each socket read, not to the whole request. Since the attacker now picks the server, this endpoint can exhaust memory or hold a worker indefinitely.
failure: `user_url` points to a multi-GB file, or to a server that sends 1 byte every 9 seconds. The worker either runs out of memory or stays blocked indefinitely (denial of service).
fix: Use `stream=True` with a maximum byte count and an overall deadline for the request.

problem: The function contract changed: the parameter used to be a relative `path` and is now a full `user_url`. Existing callers break.
failure: A caller still doing `fetch_report('reports/2026.pdf')` now gets `requests.exceptions.MissingSchema` instead of the report from api.internal.example.
fix: Keep the `path` signature and the fixed base URL, or update every caller and add validation.
